Analysis: Both hypotheses propose innovative multi-modal immunotherapy strategies aimed at converting the tumor milieu to enhance anti-tumor immunity and overcome resistance to PD-1 blockade. Hypothesis 1 is novel in its integration of real‐time imaging, transcriptomic biomarker profiling, and adaptive radiotherapy with systemic TGF-β1 and IDO inhibition. However, its plausibility is challenged by complex operational integration and uncertain dosing/timing protocols that could raise significant safety concerns. In contrast, Hypothesis 2 leverages a sequential approach combining low-dose, fractionated radiotherapy and nanoparticle-enhanced immunogenic cell death with timed PD-1 inhibition. This design, while also technically ambitious, offers a clearer sequential framework that may be more readily deconstructed and tested in staged preclinical studies. Its use of lower radiotherapy doses and defined “optimal windows” could potentially mitigate safety risks. Overall, Hypothesis 2 presents a more testable and arguably safer strategy while retaining significant novelty.
